evidence_tier: T3 POST-HOC, PROTOCOL-FIRST. Written after the T1 control verdict (NO_CONTROL_SUPERIORITY) was known. Nothing in this protocol can revise any T1 verdict.

questions.Q_A_item2b: Under the unchanged formal MPC, is the COISC-vs-R0 tracking difference (in particular the seed-20260923 gain) attributable to the lag-aware regularizer, or also produced by matched head-only fine-tuning without it (L0, lambda = 0)?
questions.Q_B_disturbance_estimation: Does the non-equivalence between sensitivity consistency and control performance persist when the MPC is given disturbance estimation from the only signals measurable in deployment (peripheral points T_1..T_6 and heater commands)? Does COISC benefit more than R0 from such estimation?

deployment_observability_constraint.fact: Author-confirmed 2026-09-29: the primary target T_p (Tp) is not measured in deployment; only T_1..T_6 are measurable.
deployment_observability_constraint.consequence: Classical offset-free MPC on T_p is not achievable in general, because a T_p offset is unobservable. The variant below is therefore called disturbance-estimating MPC (DE-MPC), not offset-free MPC. It compensates only the part of plant-model mismatch that is expressible as an equivalent constant UH input disturbance and observable through T_1..T_6.
deployment_observability_constraint.enforcement: The estimator receives only plant output[:6] and applied inputs. A unit test must assert that perturbing plant output[6] leaves every estimator output and controller decision bitwise unchanged.

controller_models.architecture: B4 Vanilla-LSTM-MS, loaded with the unchanged run_formal_control_v3a.load_model(binding, 'B4') normalization checks

variants.L0: post-hoc item-1 matched head-only fine-tuning with lambda = 0 (same optimizer, lr, steps, batches and seed as COISC)

unchanged_from_formal_control_v3: CONTROL_SCENARIO_LOCK_V2.json: 12 locked scenarios, reference 37.0 C, 60 updates of 10 s, locked background aux1/aux2/aux3/aux4/aux5, initial UH from history
CONTROL_PLANT_FAMILY_LOCK.json: primary families F1 {P,A1,A3,A4,A5} (17), F2 {A2} (3), F3 {B2} (3), F4 {B1} (1) = 24 plant checkpoints
control_mpc.py (sha 8ef305db...a08a9): MPCConfig, objective, SLSQP settings, bounds, 0.1 % quantization, warm start, apply_plant_step
primary endpoint: 600-s mean absolute plant-Tp tracking error over 60 updates
estimand: family-equal paired effect per seed, 12 source clusters; 20000-draw percentile bootstrap with rng 20260927, draws shared across contrasts, checkpoints and seeds

population.panel: primary only (24 plant checkpoints x 12 scenarios x 3 controller seeds). The secondary panels (B3, B4, V10) and oracle runs are not repeated; the formal results for those remain as reported.
population.reason_for_primary_only: All support rules in the formal plan use the primary panel; the secondary panels were descriptive. Declared before execution to bound compute.

arm_A_item2b_nominal_mpc.new_runs: L0 with the unchanged formal MPCController: 24 x 12 x 3 = 864 runs
arm_A_item2b_nominal_mpc.reused_runs: R0 and COISC primary raw runs from formal execution control_v3a_20260926T153411234230Z_0b9ad32c21, subject to gate G4

arm_B_disturbance_estimating_mpc.disturbance_model: Constant additive input disturbance d (percent of UH full scale). The internal model is evaluated with effective UH = clip(u + d, 0, 100) percent, applied to the UH channel of all 20 history frames and to all 12 future UH commands. The SLSQP decision variable, bounds, move penalty and quantization still act on u only.

estimator.type: moving-horizon estimation of the scalar d, re-solved at every update k
estimator.window: s = max(0, k - W) with W = 12 updates (120 s, equal to the MPC horizon)
estimator.prediction: internal-model open-loop rollout (rollout_native_120s) from the stored closed-loop history at update s, driven by the applied commands u_s..u_{k-1} shifted by d and by the locked background
estimator.cost: J(d) = mean over updates i in [s, k) and points j = 1..6 of (T_hat_ij(d) - T_ij_measured)^2 in C^2, plus rho * (d/100)^2 with rho = 0.01
estimator.measured_signals_used: plant output[:6] (T_1..T_6) and applied heater powers only; never plant output[6]
estimator.parameter_status: W, rho, bounds and xatol are fixed here a priori and are not tuned on any outcome. rho only makes the minimizer unique when UH is not excited within the window.

arm_B_disturbance_estimating_mpc.failure_handling: If the estimator raises or returns a non-finite value, d_hat keeps its previous value and the event is logged. MPC solver failures are handled exactly as in control_mpc.py (hold the previous command).

decision_rules.per_contrast_support: Identical to the formal plan: a contrast is SUPPORTED on a seed if the upper endpoint of the two-sided 95 % percentile CI is < 0. An overall claim requires support on all three seeds. A missing required run makes the contrast NOT_EVALUABLE.
decision_rules.multiplicity: No correction. Every contrast is reported with its per-seed CI; the 3/3 rule is the only basis for an overall statement.

interpretation_A.A1 supported on 20260923: The seed-23 gain is regularizer-specific relative to matched fine-tuning.
interpretation_A.A1 not supported on 20260923 and A2 supp: The seed-23 gain is at least partly produced by head-only fine-tuning itself, not specifically by the regularizer.
interpretation_A.A1 and A2 both not supported on 20260923: The seed-23 gain cannot be attributed to either factor.

interpretation_B.B1 supported on 3/3: Under DE-MPC, COISC gave lower tracking error than R0 on every seed (post-hoc, conditional on the MIL plant panel). This does not overturn the formal T1 verdict.
interpretation_B.B1 not supported on 3/3: Adding disturbance estimation from peripheral measurements did not produce a consistent COISC benefit; the non-equivalence finding is robust to this controller design choice.
interpretation_B.B3_X supported on 3/3: Disturbance estimation reduced tracking error for variant X.
interpretation_B.B3_X point estimate > 0 on >= 2 seeds: Report that disturbance estimation worsened tracking for variant X; do not tune or rescue.
interpretation_B.B4: Descriptive only. A negative DiD means COISC gained more than R0 from disturbance estimation; no support claim is made from B4.

forbidden: replacing or re-analysing the formal R0-vs-COISC T1 result
changing W, rho, bounds, plants, scenarios or MPC settings after any outcome is seen
reporting secondary endpoints as if they were primary
pooling seeds to override the per-seed rule

pre_execution_gates_outcome_blind.G0_hashes: All bound files (formal protocol set, control_mpc.py, L0 checkpoints, new code files) match their SHA-256 at freeze.
pre_execution_gates_outcome_blind.G1_de_disabled_equivalence: With d fixed at 0, the DE controller reproduces the nominal MPCController decisions bitwise on the first 3 updates of 3 synthetic histories built from the scenario cache (no plant outcome used).
pre_execution_gates_outcome_blind.G2_matched_plant: Plant = the internal R0 model of seed 20260922, 12 closed-loop updates on one scenario: |d_hat| < 0.1 % at every update.
pre_execution_gates_outcome_blind.G3_bias_recovery: Plant = the same internal model wrapped so that it receives UH + 10 %; 24 closed-loop updates: |d_hat - 10| <= 2 % at update 24. Failure means the estimator is not identifiable under this design; execution is then NOT authorized and any redesign requires a new protocol version that discloses this failure.
pre_execution_gates_outcome_blind.G4_reuse_reproduction: Rerun 48 formal nominal runs (for each of the 24 primary plants, scenario index = plant index mod 12, seed 20260923, both R0 and COISC) and require bitwise equality of applied_UH and plant_Tp with the stored raw runs. If equality fails, the 1728 primary R0/COISC nominal runs are rerun inside this execution and used for all contrasts; the discrepancy is reported.
pre_execution_gates_outcome_blind.G6_timing_smoke: Two DE runs on the V10 historical plant (not in the analysis population); results discarded, used only to set the worker count.

compute_plan.formal_reference_runtime: about 14 s per nominal run (2 threads), from the formal execution audit
compute_plan.new_runs: 864 nominal L0 + 2592 DE = 3456 runs (+48 for G4; +1728 if G4 fails)
compute_plan.estimated_wall_time: about 15 h serial; about 3 h with 6 worker processes x 2 threads on the 16-core machine (to be confirmed by G6)
compute_plan.parallelism: partition by plant checkpoint; each run is deterministic and written atomically; resume under the same protocol hash is allowed and logged
